messages:
Maria: Hey all — opening a PRD intake thread to capture problem, goals, non-goals and launch criteria for the per-tenant routing policy editor request from two customers.

Problem statement: multiple customers are asking for the ability to define routing rules per tenant so they can send low-latency traffic to dedicated pools, route heavy batch traffic to cheaper instances, and have explicit fallbacks when a model variant is unavailable. Right now routing is global and encoded in infra config; customers want a UI + API to make these rules tenant-scoped without engineering help.

Goals:
- Provide a tenant-level routing editor (UI + API) that supports rules based on: model family, latency target, cost tier, and region.
- Allow policies to be evaluated at request time with deterministic fallback order.
- Support safe rollouts: canary rules, A/B buckets, and automatic fallback to global policy.
- Expose observability: per-rule hit counts, avg latency, and cost delta per token.

Non-goals:
- This does NOT include fine-grained token-level reranking or rewriting (that stays in model layer).
- We will not ship advanced policy language in v1 (no full DSL). v1 will be constrained predicates only.

Success metrics (first pass):
- 3 pilot customers onboarded within 8 weeks.
- Average query-level routing time added < 8ms p50 and < 25ms p99.
- No correctness regressions in model outputs attributable to routing (tracked via eval harness smoke tests).
- Customers report perceived control increase (qualitative) and we see a 30% reduction in engineering support tickets for routing-related asks.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- API: POST/GET/PUT/DELETE for tenant policies with schema validation and per-tenant isolation.
- UI: routing editor shows policy graph, fallback chain, and last 24h rule hits; can create a canary (specify percentage) and promote/rollback.
- Runtime: outbound request routing decision must be deterministic and recorded in request trace (trace tag `routing.policy_id`).
- Observability: dashboard tile for each tenant with rule hit counts and latency buckets; alert when a rule's CPU-backed path exceeds configured cost threshold.
- Security: tenant policies only visible to tenant admins; audit log entry created for policy changes.

Edge cases we've to consider:
- Conflicting rules (overlapping predicates) — need deterministic tie-breaker (priority + creation time). Proposal: higher `priority` wins, tie by `created_at`.
- What happens when dedicated pool is out of capacity? Must fallback to next policy and mark the rule as degraded; include automatic backoff + retry logic.
- Multi-region requests with geo-preference vs. model availability mismatch — prefer region affinity unless model latency would break SLO.
- Hot-swap model variants mid-request: ensure routing uses pinned variant if request references a pinned model version.

Questions for eng/infra:
Sam: Is the proposed p99 routing decision overhead budget (25ms) achievable if we include policy evaluation + auth checks + trace emission? Any memory/CPU concerns for continuous evaluation at high QPS?
Sam: Also need clarity on how policies are stored —MDS? etc. Can we piggyback on existing tenant config storage?

Sam: Short answer — policy evaluation is cheap if we keep predicates simple (exact match, prefix, numeric thresholds). Biggest cost will be trace emission and any RPCs to capacity service. We should avoid sync calls for capacity checks; instead use cached pool health + a soft TTL and degrade gracefully.

Alex: From ML side — we need to ensure that fallback model variants are compatible (same tokenizer/sequence lengths) or we risk decode issues. Acceptance criteria should include compatibility checks and automated conversion hints in UI.

Kevin: UX note — for v1 please keep the editor compact: rules list + conditions + priority + canary rollout. Defer policy simulation to v2. Non-goal: no WYSIWYG flowchart in v1.

Jenna: SRE concerns — can we add a safety circuit that auto-throws to a global safe policy if routing evaluation fails for >1% of requests in a minute? We should protect tenants from local bugs causing widespread failures.

Maria: Agree on the safety circuit. Proposed behavior: on failure-rate breach, mark tenant routing as "degraded" and route to global safe policy; emit incident metric and create an audit event.

Sam: For storage, we'll reuse tenant-config service (keyed by tenant_id) with an additional policy schema version. We'll add an in-memory cache with invalidation on change events. That should keep latency low.

Alex: Will add model compatibility check in onboarding flow: when a tenant points a rule to a model variant, we run a compatibility probe asynchronously; UI shows status: `compatible`, `incompatible`, or `pending`.

Maria: Launch criteria (v1):
- All acceptance tests green in staging for 72h, including chaos testing where we simulate pool OOMs.
- Two pilot customers complete onboarding and run production load for at least 1 week.
- Documentation + runbook published.
- GA checklist: security review completed, and pricing decision for dedicated routing tier.

Kevin: One more UX constraint — keep terminology consistent with Console (use "Policy" not "Rule" everywhere).

Sam: Implementation plan outline (very high level):
- Week 0–2: schema + API + storage hookup.
- Week 3–5: runtime evaluation path + cache + trace tagging.
- Week 6: UI prototype + basic observability tiles.
- Week 7–8: pilot onboarding + hardening.

Maria: Prioritization ask — we have capacity in H1 to run this as a focused sprint if product backs it. If we need to defer, let's list minimum viable subset: API + runtime evaluation + global fallback (no UI). That gives customers API-only control.

Sam: Concern — we have infra tech debt from the batching cache refactor. If we overlap that work we might need extra heads. Flagging for PMs.

Maria: Ok. Action items:
- Sam: produce rough perf budget and confirm 25ms p99 routing budget is feasible (due EOD Tue).
- Alex: draft compatibility probe spec and list basic checks (tokenizer, max_seq_len, dtype compatibility) (due Fri).
- Kevin: mockups for editor v1 (due Thu).
- Jenna: add SRE safety circuit proposal to oncall runbook (due next Wed).
- Maria: I'll assemble a short PRD doc from this thread and run it by infra/product leadership.

prd-bot: Note — created tracker PRD-3812 and assigned to Maria.

Sam: ack. I'll start with a microbenchmark and post results here.

Kevin: :thumbsup:

Maria: Thanks everyone — ping me if anything missing.
